text:
Meal: Dinner

Rationale: After drinking at Reservoir, I was starving. Casa Tapas was the closest place on my list of vegetarian-suitable restaurants in Montreal as gleaned from Chowhound.com. And I just think tapas is neat.

Food: Small plates, kind of pricey, nothing unexpected. In order of appearance: (0) We had red wine. I forget what kind. Probably French or Italian. It was fine. (1) Free bread. Immediately. Lots and lots of free bread. And free olives. And probably free olive oil. I don't remember that particular detail. When I'd finish the free bread and free olives, more would appear by magic. Instantaneously. Without asking. Even while we were eating the other food. (2) Gazpacho. Not too oily, not too watery, well-balanced, but nothing to write home about. (3) Champiñones al ajillo [garlic mushrooms]. If I remember correctly, this wasn't just a bowl of mushrooms. It was mushrooms on top of something white. Maybe that was the garlic component, somehow. But it was delicious. Either we ate it on the bread, or we ate it with a fork and then used the bread to scoop up every last drop. At any rate, thank heavens for the free bread, which we probably finished with the champiñones and saw instantly replenished. (4) Espárragos al manchego [asparagus with manchego cheese]. A few stalks of grilled (or maybe sauteed) asparagus with flakes of manchego on top. Exactly what it said on the label. Fine. Give me more champiñones. (5) Berenjenas rellenas [stuffed eggplant]. Kind of bland. Eggplant is a difficult vegetable to cook right, and it's got a delicate flavour that is easily overwhelmed or watered down. This case was the latter. I don't remember what it was stuffed with (more eggplant?) but it didn't really taste like anything. I should have known better than to order eggplant. Forgive me, I may have been drunk. (6) MORE FREE BREAD.

Service/atmosphere: Kind of had a traditional ""fine dining"" feel to it, given the white tablecloths, server uniforms, and so forth, plus some borderline-gaudy mediterranean decor, plus some avant-garde single-blade ceiling fans. Not really my style (I prefer it toned down a bit). If the bread situation is any indication, service was prompt and continuous and professional, if a little bit mechanical (my boyfriend commented that it was almost like an assembly line...cold and impersonal...but I don't really mind).

Conclusion: A few hits, a few misses. Such is the nature of tapas. I'd try a few more tapases if I was up to spending the money. Or I'd just order a dozen Champiñones.
manual_explanation: The review contains both strong positives and negatives across food, price, service, and atmosphere. The final recommendation is only mildly positive, leaving the example close to the decision boundary.
testable_fix: Use hierarchical or sentence-level aggregation for long reviews and test aspect-aware sentiment pooling.

I've now made three trips to Lobby's.  The first was an enormous disappointment, the last two have been exceptional.

On my first trip, I made the mistake of ordering the Italian beef sandwich.  What I received could best be described as a thinly-sliced beef sandwich on a baguette that some jerk spilled soup on.  My sandwich was soggy to the point of disintegration from the moment I received it.  I tend to be a very neat eater, but felt I needed a bib that day.  In addition to the mess, the whole assemblage was bland and unremarkable.  

However...

I'd happily recommend Lobby's to anyone who wants a burger.  Upon hearing great things about their hamburgers, I returned to Lobby on two more occcasions.  On both days, I got a ridiculously large, juicy burger with great quality beef and fresh ingredients for a price around half of their competitors (I'm looking at you, Smashburger and Five Guys).  

So, go for the burgers and read the menu carefully: the single patty burger is 1/3 pound.  If you order the double, you're ordering more than a half-pound of beef and you will need a nap.
manual_explanation: The review opens with a strongly negative first visit, then uses 'However' to describe two later exceptional visits and ultimately recommends the burgers. The model struggles to weight the later positive evidence enough.
testable_fix: Test hierarchical sentence pooling or attention over discourse segments so later conclusion/recommendation sentences receive appropriate weight.
